chief_complaint: large fluid swelling over elbow tip, painless and non-red
hpi_details: 45-year-old male presents with a large, fluctuant swelling over the posterior aspect of his right elbow. It is painless, non-erythematous, and not warm to touch. He is a plumber and frequently leans on his elbows at work. Full range of motion of the elbow joint is preserved.
ideas: He thinks he burst a small fluid sac or formed a cyst from constantly resting his elbow on hard pipes under sinks.
concerns: He is worried that he will need surgery that could put him out of work and cause him to lose plumbing clients.
expectations: He hopes the doctor can drain the fluid with a needle today and bandage it so he can get right back to work.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Olecranon bursitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Olecranon Bursitis: Elbow pad to protect, compress dressing, avoid aspiration if uninfected, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: large fluid swelling over elbow tip, painless and non-red

45-year-old male presents with a large, fluctuant swelling over the posterior aspect of his right elbow. It is painless, non-erythematous, and not warm to touch. He is a plumber and frequently leans on his elbows at work. Full range of motion of the elbow joint is preserved.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals normal. Right elbow exam reveals a 4 cm discrete, soft, cystic, fluctuant mass over the olecranon bursa. No overlying erythema, warmth, or tenderness. Full active and passive ROM.
reference_soap.plan: Reassurance. Advise use of elbow pads to prevent repetitive trauma. Aspiration not indicated unless suspecting infection. NSAIDs PRN.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Olecranon Bursitis
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Olecranon Bursitis
Implement evidence-based management plan: Elbow pad to protect, compress dressing, avoid aspiration if uninfected

teaching.one_liner: Patient with a large, painless, non-red fluid swelling over the tip of the elbow.
red_flags: Redness, warmth, or fever would suggest septic bursitis requiring aspiration and antibiotics

must_ask.say: Is the swelling painful, red, or warm to touch?

must_ask.objective: Ask about recent trauma or pressure
must_ask.say: Have you been leaning on your elbow a lot, or had any recent injury to it?
Do you have any fever or feel unwell?
Do you have gout or rheumatoid arthritis?

must_ask.objective: Explain the protective and conservative treatment plan
must_ask.say: We recommend protecting the elbow with a pad and compression, avoiding drainage unless it becomes infected.

history.answer: I've got this big, squishy fluid lump that popped up on the tip of my right elbow.
I first noticed it about two weeks ago, and it has stayed swollen ever since.
It is right on the very back tip of my right elbow.
It started out as a small bump and gradually swelled up over a couple of weeks to about the size of a golf ball.
It is just this single lump on my right elbow. I do not have any lumps anywhere else.
It feels very soft and squishy, kind of like a water balloon under my skin, and I can wiggle it around slightly.
No, there is no pain at all. It does not hurt even when I press directly on it.
No, the skin over it looks completely normal, with no dark spots, sores, or unusual moles.
No, it has never bled, and there are no scabs or open sores on it.
No, it is not red at all, and it does not feel warm to the touch.
No, there is no hole, pus, or foul-smelling drainage coming out of it.
It feels a bit more swollen and tight at the end of a long workday after I have been leaning on it.
I haven't had any sudden injuries or cuts there, but as a plumber, I spend hours crawling and resting my elbows on hard floors.
No, I've never had any cuts, surgeries, piercings, or severe skin infections in that spot.
No, I have not had any fevers, chills, night sweats, or unexpected weight loss.
I work indoors doing plumbing under sinks and in basements, and I have never had any severe sunburns.
No, neither I nor anyone in my family has ever had skin cancer or abnormal moles.
No, I don't have diabetes, I've never had an organ transplant, and I don't take any immune-suppressing medications.
No, I haven't tried popping it, squeezing it, or draining it with a needle, and I haven't seen a doctor for it yet.
I can bend and straighten my elbow all the way without any stiffness, catching, or pain.
No, I've never had gout, painful swollen joints, or rheumatoid arthritis.
No, I haven't felt any swollen lymph nodes or tender glands anywhere on my body.
I wondered if I popped a fluid sac or built up a cyst from constantly leaning my elbow on hard pipes while doing plumbing work.
I'm really worried that this might need surgery, which would keep me off the job and cost me work.
I'm hoping you can just draw the fluid out with a needle and wrap it up so I can get back to work today.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions or health problems.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital stays.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, or supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications.
I am a non-smoker and have never smoked.
I am a social drinker and only have a couple of beers on weekends.
I work as a plumber and live at home with my wife.
My parents and siblings are healthy with no major medical illnesses.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 bpm, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6 °C, SpO2 99% on room air.
Well-nourished male in no acute distress, resting comfortably.

A 4 cm discrete, soft, mobile, fluctuant fluid-filled swelling over the right olecranon bursa with normal overlying skin, no erythema, warmth, ulceration, central punctum, or abnormal pigmentation, and no suspicious lesions elsewhere.
Right elbow examination reveals swelling confined strictly to the olecranon bursa with no joint effusion, no warmth, no tenderness to palpation, and full active and passive range of motion.
Full 5/5 motor strength in bilateral elbow flexion, extension, wrist, and hand muscles.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation throughout the right upper extremity, including radial, median, and ulnar nerve distributions.
No palpable cervical, supraclavicular, or axillary lymphadenopathy.
